query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a thin, uniform coating of a self-lubricating 2D high-entropy alloy (HEA) phase, similar in composition to (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2, onto a CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix will maintain low friction and wear rates across a broad temperature range (RT to 800 °C) compared to the uncoated alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix with baseline high friction and wear performance at high temperatures.
generation.intervention: Apply a thin, uniform coating of a 2D self-lubricating HEA phase, such as (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2, on the wear surface of the CoCrFeNi HEA.
generation.conditions: Sliding experiments performed under varying operating temperatures ranging from room temperature (RT) to 800 °C, at controlled loads (high contact pressures similar to those used in prior studies) and in ambient or moderately oxidizing environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a shear-induced lubricious tribofilm mediated by the 2D HEA coating, which promotes tribocatalytic activity and continuous regeneration of a protective layer on the CoCrFeNi surface.
generation.mechanism: Under sliding, the coating undergoes shear-induced transformations that promote energy dissipation and tribocatalytic reactions. This dynamically forms a lubricious film at the interface, reducing friction and wear. The self-replenishing nature of this film helps maintain performance across a wide range of temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the uncoated CoCrFeNi alloy, the coated system is expected to exhibit significantly reduced coefficients of friction and lower wear rates throughout the temperature range (RT to 800 °C), with values approaching those observed in related studies (e.g., around 0.076 friction coefficient under high contact pressures).
generation.baseline: CoCrFeNi HEA without the 2D HEA coating tested under identical temperature, load, and environmental conditions.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are expected under a wide temperature range (RT to 800 °C) and under the applied loads that generate high contact stresses; performance may vary if environmental conditions (e.g., severe oxidizing atmospheres) or dynamic load cycles are significantly altered from those used in prior studies.
generation.uncertainty: The durability and stability of the tribofilm at extreme temperatures, and its behavior under varying sliding speeds and loads, require further investigation. The exact magnitude of friction and wear reduction may vary based on coating adherence and the detailed microstructural interactions at the interface.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of CoCrFeNi HEA substrates coated with the 2D HEA (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 phase and one set of uncoated CoCrFeNi. Perform ball-on-disk tribological tests under identical conditions across temperatures ranging from RT to 800 °C under controlled high contact pressures and ambient atmospheric conditions. Record the coefficients of friction and wear rates for all samples.
measurements: Coefficient of friction (as a function of temperature)
Surface analysis post-test (to identify the formation and integrity of the tribofilm)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in both coefficient of friction and wear rate across the tested temperature range compared to the uncoated baseline, or if the tribofilm fails to form/maintain integrity under the prescribed conditions, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractHigh Entropy Alloys (HEAs) have garnered attention due to their remarkable tribological attributes. Predominantly, failure mechanisms in HEAs emanate from stress‐induced dislocations, culminating in crack propagation and film delamination. In this study, we report on the synthesis of 2D HEA of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 which facilitates shear‐induced energy dissipation at sliding interfaces. The ball‐on‐disk tribological investigations demonstrate unprecedentedly low average coefficients of friction (0.076) and wear rates (10−9 mm3 (N∙m)−1) under high contact pressures (0.936 GPa) within ambient conditions. Employing multi‐scale characterizations alongside molecular dynamic simulations, we elucidate that the presence of the HEA triggers tribocatalytic activity under high contact pressures emerging as a pivotal factor in extending lubricant lifespan during tribological tests. The resilient lubriciousness coupled with the facile spray coating methodology of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 in ambient environments paves the way for the development of a new class of solid lubricants based on 2D HEA.
